grading_system.evidence: Graduation requirements are met by earning a total of 24 proficiency credits in the required content areas indicated below. Beginning 2026-2027, course proficiency credit is earned by achieving a 2.0 or higher in a course academic mastery score and a course transferable skill mastery score.
grading_system.proficiency_scale: 4 Extending, 3 Proficient, 2 Developing, 1 Getting Started, U Insufficient Evidence
grading_system.min_score_to_earn_credit: 2.0 in both academic mastery and transferable skill mastery

schedule.evidence: Mt. Abraham works on a rotating schedule of Maroon (M) and White (W) days ... Block 1M/1W through Block 4M/4W (four blocks each day, so eight classes across the rotation). The catalog also says 'VHS is a class scheduled into a student's 8 block rotation.'

credit_definition.text: Requirements are counted in proficiency credits. The catalog states a credit value for some courses (for example, AP courses are 'a full year, one credit course'), but does not state a credit value for each semester course. Credit is awarded at 0.5 credits per semester of college coursework in the dual enrollment note.
credit_definition.evidence: Advanced Placement European History is a full year, one credit course that introduces students to European History

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: The catalog calls these 24 proficiency credits (7.5 elective or choice). Area requirements: Literacy 4, Social Studies 3.5, Mathematics 3, Science 3, Physical Education 1.5, Health Education 0.5, Artistic Expression 1 (World Language not required). Catalog gives no conversion from proficiency credits to standard credits (1 = full-year course), so total_in_credits is null. Also requires a Personalized Learning Plan (PLP) and PLP exhibition.

notes: Catalog is the 2026-27 Program of Studies. Graduation is proficiency-based (PBGRs, p.4-5): 24 proficiency credits, 2.0 minimum in both academic mastery and transferable skill mastery per course, and a PLP exhibition. The four transferable skill areas are Personal Development, Community Connections, Innovative Thinking and Effective Communication (p.4). Full-time status requires 6 courses per semester (p.53). Schedule uses M/W days with four blocks each day, plus an advisory and FIT block (p.15). The catalog does not state the number of semester-course credits per course; the conversion for college courses is 0.5 credit per semester (p.10). Some HS courses are marked as full year, and the catalog does not give standard credits for each course.
